name: Jotform
description: Jotform submissions become Form Submitted events on the respondent's profile, with the answers you choose to copy. Jotform's webhooks aren't signed, so DumbMail fetches each submission from Jotform's API and keeps only the email, a consent question you map and those answers. A submission never subscribes anyone.

credentials.name: api_key
credentials.label: Jotform API key
credentials.help: Jotform → My Account → API → Create New Key (Read Access). Used to fetch each submission a webhook names.

setup: Create the integration from this recipe and copy its webhook URL. Keep it private: Jotform doesn't sign webhooks, so the URL is the secret.

In Jotform, open My Account → API → Create New Key with Read Access, and save it as the credential api_key. If your account is on Jotform's EU servers, change api.jotform.com to eu-api.jotform.com in the Pull tab (hipaa-api.jotform.com for HIPAA accounts).
Open the form in the Form Builder → Settings → Integrations → Webhooks, paste the webhook URL and complete the integration.

Set form_id in the integration's settings to the form's ID (the number in its address); submissions from other forms are ignored. Set email_field to the ID of the form's email question. The question IDs are the numbers in https://api.jotform.com/form/<form ID>/questions?apiKey=<your key>.

If the form asks for marketing consent, set consent_field to that question's ID and consent_value to the exact answer that means yes (for example "Yes, send me emails"): it's recorded on each Form Submitted event as marketing_consent. Set copy_fields to the IDs of the answers worth keeping on the event, for example ["5", "7"]. Nothing else from a submission is stored.
Send a test submission and check the delivery log: the webhook is followed by a fetch of the submission.

People this adds are held back from marketing. A form submission isn't an opt-in (anyone can type an address into a form), so nobody is subscribed. To add people who ticked the consent question to your marketing, send them a confirmation (double opt-in) first.
